messages.subject: [rkward-users] Compatibility between RKWard and RGtk2
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

On Monday 31 August 2009, Nicolas Chapados wrote:
> I'm a new RKWard user and so far I've been quite pleased with the
> environment it provides for R development.

thanks!

> However, I'm wondering if
> the compatibility with RGtk2 has been tested.

Well, tested, yes. We are aware of this issue, but it is not easy to fix. I do 
have an idea on how to approach - and hopefully fix - this problem and a few 
related ones. But this will need a good deal of work, and other things are 
higher up in priority ATM.

Last time I checked, version 0.4.9b of RKWard (based on KDE/Qt 3) was not 
affected. While this version does not have some of the most recent features, 
perhaps this is an option for you.

See also 
https://sourceforge.net/tracker/?func=detail&aid=1878594&group_id=50231&atid=459007 
. This describes slightly different symptoms, but I'm fairly sure that it's the 
same underlying issue.

Regards
Thomas

hi corrado,

am Freitag, 4. September 2009 (09:38) schrieb Corrado:
> I have difficulties installing any plugin. What is the procedure,
> exactly???? My lists are all empty!

out of the blue i'd say the path to all.pluginmap is not configured correctly:
  preferences -> configure rkward -> plugins
check the .pluginmap files, on my kubuntu 9.04 it reads

  /usr/share/kde4/apps/rkward/all.pluginmap

> kubuntu 904 64 bit + kde 424 + rkward 050d.

you could add this repo and upgrade to 0.5.1:
http://sourceforge.net/apps/mediawiki/rkward/index.php?title=Binaries_and_Build_Scripts#Unofficial_Ubuntu_repositories

messages.body_plain:
Hi!

I'd like to conduct a quick informal survey to determine whether/when further 
backports to KDE 3 are needed.

1) Are you still using RKWard for KDE 3 (i.e. RKWard 0.4.9x or lower)?

(No need to respond if the answer is "no").

2) If so, which version of R do you use with that?

3) Are there any specific reasons that keep you from upgrading?

Thanks!

Regards
Thomas

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

On 9/30/09, Thomas Friedrichsmeier
<thomas.friedrichsmeier at ruhr-uni-bochum.de> wrote:
> Hi!
>
> I'd like to conduct a quick informal survey to determine whether/when
> further
> backports to KDE 3 are needed.
>
> 1) Are you still using RKWard for KDE 3 (i.e. RKWard 0.4.9x or lower)?

YES. (rkward 0.4.9b, OR the relevant svn branch - depending on developments)

> (No need to respond if the answer is "no").

Statistically, it is important to get the "no" responses too ;)

> 2) If so, which version of R do you use with that?

Currently, R 2.8.2, but this updates from time to time....

> 3) Are there any specific reasons that keep you from upgrading?

Yes: no control over the department's servers. They use RedHat EL,
currently at 5.3.

[Aside:
I am not sure if RedHat EL 6 will include KDE 4, though SLE 11.0
already has KDE 4.1.3. Do any universities in US (or anywhere else for
that matter) use Canonical for their enterprise Linux solutions?]

> Thanks!
>
> Regards
> Thomas

Thanks for keeping KDE3 port alive. I can totally understand if you
decide not to in future (if yes/(no+yes) << 1).

Regards
-- 
Prasenjit
